subject: Discovery recap & PoC plan — FastRetail integration

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & PoC plan — FastRetail integration

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed PoC plan so we’re aligned on scope and next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

1) Key pain points you shared
- Search relevancy degrades for product catalog updates (re-index latency + embeddings mismatch)
- High per-token inference costs on current endpoint during peak shopping windows
- Need predictable latency for customer-facing recommendations (p90 < 120ms)

2) Current stack
- GCP (BigQuery for analytics, GCS for artifacts)
- Recommendation service in Node.js, currently calling hosted LLM endpoints (pay-as-you-go)
- No existing caching layer for token-level reuse

3) Success criteria for PoC (what FastRetail wants to validate)
- End-to-end latency p90 < 120ms for the recommendation call in production-like load
- Matching or better recommendation quality vs current baseline (A/B eval set)
- 30% reduction in per-unit cost for inference at target throughput

4) Integration & onboarding details
- SDK languages: primary = Node.js (server runtime), secondary = Python for offline evals
- API compatibility: Redwood’s REST/SDK will be used; we support OpenAI-compatible endpoints and a Node SDK that plugs in with minimal changes
- Authentication: API Key + optional mTLS for Dedicated/Private later

5) Proposed PoC milestones (6 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff + access + test dataset (owner: Alex)
- Week 1: Basic integration and smoke tests using Node SDK (owner: Ben)
- Week 2-3: Load testing and latency tuning (batching, cache) (owner: Ben)
- Week 4: Quality evaluation vs baseline (owner: Marissa)
- Week 5-6: Finalize runbook, cost analysis, exec recap (owner: Vanessa)

6) Deliverables we’ll provide
- Integration checklist + sample Node integration (redwood-poc-mrp.yml attached)
- SDK compatibility matrix (attached)
- Preliminary cost/latency estimate and configuration recommendations (we’ll share after initial smoke test)

Next steps
- Alex to share sample dataset and a technical contact for the deep-dive (Olivia if available) — target: by Mon 7/6
- We’ll schedule a 60-min tech deep dive next week (Ben + Marissa + FastRetail eng)
- I’ll send a draft SOW for review (Vanessa)

Attachments: redwood-poc-mrp.yml, redwood-sdk-compatibility-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Alex / team — Ben here (SE) — looping in a few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive.

Quick answers:
- Node SDK: our Node SDK (v2) supports streams and auto-batching; it’s drop-in for typical request flows and requires ~15 lines of change to the recommendation call.
- Python: we’ll provide a sample client for offline evals and model comparison.
- Retention: hosted mode default logs retention = 90 days; for PoC we can set 14-day retention and redact sensitive fields — we’ll capture requirements during kickoff.
- SOC 2 + encryption: we can provide the SOC 2 assessment summary and KMS integration docs prior to kickoff (sending links in the deep-dive invite).

Recommended PoC approach (short):
1) Start with smoke integration in staging using Node SDK (1-2 days)
2) Enable prefix/KV caching for product descriptions to reduce token reuse and improve p90 latency
3) Run a controlled load test (throughput target: 400 RPS peak) and tune batching window
4) Run the quality eval in Week 4 against the A/B set provided by FastRetail

I’ve attached the compatibility matrix and an example runbook (redwood-sdk-compatibility-matrix.xlsx, fastretail-sow-draft.pdf). For the deep-dive, please include your infra/ops person that manages the staging GCP project so we can talk permissions.

If Thu 7/9 10:00 PT works, I’ll send the calendar invite and attach the SOC2 summary + KMS doc.

Thanks,
